how.title: How GigoMe works
how.lead: GigoMe lists paid part-time jobs and gigs in Milan that you can do in English. You find a job here, then contact the employer directly: GigoMe isn't part of the application or the work.
how.aside: Some jobs mean meeting an employer at an address. <link>Read Staying safe</link>.
how.findA1: Browse the list or the map on the <link>Jobs</link> page: you don't need an account for that. Filter by area, category, when the work happens, pay, hours, languages and how much Italian you need.
how.findA2: Log in to save jobs and searches and to follow companies. They stay on GigoMe: we don't email you about them.
how.emailQ: Do I need a university email?
how.emailA1: No, any email works. GigoMe is for university students, and a student email from a university on our list verifies that you're a student. To see the list, open "Which emails verify you as a student?" on the <link>student login</link>. With any other email, you tell us after logging in that you're a university student and which university; we don't check that answer.
how.emailA2: When you log in, we send a 6-digit code to your email; there's no password. The code only shows that you can read that inbox. It doesn't check that you're enrolled or that you're allowed to work in Italy. Is your university missing from the list? Write to {email}.
how.applyA1: GigoMe shows you how to apply for that job, the employer's application page or email address, and opens it. You then contact the employer directly, outside GigoMe. GigoMe doesn't send them your profile, your CV or anything else, and pressing Apply isn't an application.
how.applyA2: GigoMe records that your account pressed Apply on that job, and when. You see it under "Jobs you opened" on your Saved jobs page. The employer only sees how many times Apply was pressed on their job, never by whom. Within 180 days, the record no longer shows who pressed it.
how.seesQ: What does GigoMe see, and what doesn't it?
how.seesA1: GigoMe sees your email, your university (from your university email, or as you told us), name, degree and graduation year; the jobs you save, your saved searches and the companies you follow; which jobs you pressed Apply on; and any reports or feedback you send. It also keeps the technical records needed to run the site. The <link>Privacy Notice</link> has the full list.
how.seesA2: GigoMe doesn't see your applications, your CV or your messages to employers, whether you had an interview or got the job, or anything you agree with an employer.
how.seesA3: Employers can't see or search your profile. They never get your name or email from GigoMe.
how.deleteQ: How do I delete my account?
how.deleteA1: Open your <link>Account</link> page (your name in the header) and press "Delete my account", then type DELETE. Your account is deleted straight away. You can press "Download my data" first to keep a copy.
how.deleteA2: Some records stay without your name, such as that Apply was pressed on a job, or a report you sent. Anything you sent to an employer stays with them. You can also write to {email}.
how.signupA1: Go to <link>For employers</link> and log in with your work email. We send you a 6-digit code; there's no password. University email addresses are for student accounts, and each email has one role: an email that already has a student account can't also be an employer account.
how.signupA2: Then tell us about your company: its name, website and a short description, and a contact email that only the GigoMe team sees. Tick the box to accept the Terms. Listing jobs is free.
how.reviewQ: How does the company review work?
how.reviewA1: A person at GigoMe reviews every new company before its jobs can go live, usually within 2 working days. Your dashboard shows the status: In review, Approved or Not approved. We don't email you when it changes.
how.reviewA2: While you wait, you can write your jobs as drafts. Only you can see them.
how.postQ: How do I post a job?
how.postA1: On your dashboard, press "New job". GigoMe lists paid part-time jobs and gigs only: no internships and no unpaid work.
how.postA2: Say what the work is, where and when it happens, the hours, the pay (per hour, per month or per project) and how students apply: a link to your application page or an email address.
how.postA3: A job is shown for up to 60 days. While it's live, and up to 14 days after it ends, you can extend it by 60 days without a new review.
how.jobReviewQ: Is every job reviewed before it's published?
how.jobReviewA1: Yes. Once your company is approved, submit each job: a person at GigoMe reviews it before students see it, usually within 2 working days.
how.jobReviewA2: We check that the role is clearly described, that pay and hours are stated, that nothing is asked of students up front (no fees, deposits or documents), and that nothing in it looks discriminatory or unlawful. If something needs fixing, we ask for changes with a note on your dashboard. Editing a live job sends it back to review.
how.contactA1: Students who press Apply see the application link or email address you gave for that job, and contact you directly. GigoMe doesn't forward applications or CVs and isn't part of the hiring.
how.contactA2: You handle applications yourself, and the written terms and other obligations of any work you agree (<link>Terms</link>, sections 9 to 11). You can't see student profiles. Your dashboard shows how many times Apply was pressed on each job, never by whom.
how.more: More questions? Write to {email}. See also <safety>Staying safe</safety>, the <terms>Terms</terms> and the <privacy>Privacy Notice</privacy>.
safety.title: Staying safe
safety.lead: Some jobs mean meeting an employer at an address you don't know. Here's what GigoMe checks, what it can't, and how to look after yourself.
safety.check1: Every company is reviewed by a person at GigoMe before its jobs can go live. We compare its login email, website and description.
safety.check2: Every job is reviewed by a person before students see it. We check that the role is clearly described, that pay and hours are stated, that nothing is asked of students up front, and that nothing in it looks discriminatory or unlawful.
safety.check3: Every report is read by a person. We can take a job down, or remove a company and all its jobs.
safety.limit1: A review checks what the employer tells us. It can't verify every employer or show that every listing is genuine or lawful (<link>Terms, section 15.2</link>).
safety.limit2: GigoMe isn't part of the work. It doesn't supervise any job, isn't a party to what you agree with an employer, and can't guarantee pay or how anyone behaves (<link>Terms, section 19</link>).
safety.limit3: So follow the tips below for every job, even one that looks fine.
safety.tip1: Never pay to get a job. No registration fees, deposits, training you pay for or kits you must buy. If anyone asks, stop and report the job.
safety.tip2: Look the business up before you go: its website, its reviews and the address on a map. Check that the name and the place match the listing.
safety.tip3: Meeting at an address for the first time? Tell someone where you're going and when you'll be back, and go during the business's opening hours.
safety.tip4: Get the essential terms in writing before you start: what you'll do, the hours, the place, the pay and the type of contract (Terms, section 8.1).
safety.tip5: Unpaid "trial shifts" doing real work are a red flag. Work should be paid.
safety.tip6: Never share passwords or login codes. GigoMe never asks for your login code.
safety.tip7: Keep your bank details to yourself until you have the written terms of a real job. An employer needs your bank account only to pay you, and never needs your card number or PIN.
safety.tip8: From outside the EU? Check how many hours your residence permit lets you work on an official source, such as the Italian government's portal for migrants, or ask your university's international office.
safety.wrong1: On the job's page, press "Report this job" (you need to be logged in). A person at GigoMe reads every report.
